author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose texture-cache corruption after a renderer crash
summary: Distinguish stale disposable graphics data from damaged game files or saves by restarting Android, reproducing on the system driver, rebuilding only documented cache once, and proving later cold launches remain clean.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Vulkan hardware OSD showing hash-cache use during a graphics-cache investigation

sourceLabels.android-cache: Android cache and app-specific storage boundaries

blocks.text: Prove the fault began with retained graphics state

A driver or renderer crash can leave the next launch with scrambled textures, stale targets, or a compile failure, but the same symptoms can come from a damaged image, texture pack, or save state. Record the first clean session, the crash event, and the first corrupted cold launch. Determine whether the fault affects one title, one scene, or every game before touching stored data.
Never clear complete app data for a cache experiment. Memory cards, in-game saves, profiles, firmware references, and library permissions are not disposable graphics cache.

items: The app's documented cache-clear action or exact disposable directory.
Backups of title profiles, memory cards, and normal saves.
A verified personal game image and system GPU driver.
Screenshots from before and after the renderer crash.
A clean title that can act as a control.

blocks.text: Restart first, rebuild cache once, then stop

items: 1. Force-stop EmuCoreX, restart Android, and wait for storage to mount before reopening the title.
2. Run the affected scene on the system driver with texture replacements disabled.
3. Launch the control title; a fault across unrelated games strengthens the retained-renderer-state hypothesis.
4. Use only the documented graphics-cache clear action and record exactly what it removes.
5. Cold-boot the affected title and allow one complete shader or texture rebuild without repeated restarts.
6. Close normally and launch the same scene twice more.
7. Verify the personal image hash and clean in-game save when corruption remains.
8. Restore optional texture packs or custom drivers one at a time only after the clean path passes.

blocks.text: Disposable cache can be regenerated; user content cannot. A one-time rebuild followed by stable later launches supports the cache diagnosis. Repeated corruption after clean generation points toward the driver, storage, replacement assets, or an emulator regression instead of justifying endless deletion.
Cache recovery passes only when stability persists without further cleaning.

items: Textures and render targets rebuild correctly on the first clean launch.
Two later cold launches show the same correct scene.
The control title remains unaffected.
Image hashes, saves, memory cards, and profiles are unchanged.
The accepted path uses the documented driver and cache policy.

blocks.text: Symptoms that reject a cache-only diagnosis

items: Corruption returns after every crash: isolate renderer and driver lifecycle.
Only a texture pack fails: validate its manifest and source files separately.
One game image fails across clean devices: verify or re-dump the personal disc.
An emulator save state restores the fault: reproduce from a normal in-game save.

blocks.text: Restore optional layers after the clean baseline

Keep the newly generated disposable cache, restore the backed-up title profile without custom drivers or packs, and cold-boot once. Reintroduce each optional layer separately; remove the first one that recreates corruption.

The operating system can delete cache under storage pressure. A correct design must rebuild safely, but frequent eviction can cause repeated compilation. Preserve free space and do not store irreplaceable user data in cache.
